title: Why Redis is fast

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Data lives in memory, so reads and writes avoid disk. Its data structures are simple and purpose-built, such as hashes and skip lists, and commands are short. Command execution is single-threaded, so there are no locks and no context switches between commands. It uses I/O multiplexing (epoll or kqueue) to serve many clients from one thread. Network round trips, not command cost, usually limit throughput, so pipelining helps.

points.title: In-memory data
points.why: Memory access is much faster than disk, which is the biggest factor.

points.title: No locks for commands
points.why: Single-threaded command execution avoids locking and context switching.

points.title: I/O multiplexing
points.why: One thread watches many sockets with epoll or kqueue.
